notes: Direct curl_cffi HTTP fetch worked for every URL (no WAF). Found a genuine company-wide umbrella page uk/New-In/c/all-new-in ('All New In') plus 14 department-scoped 'new-in' nodes via uk/sitemap_Category.xml keyword sweep for 'new-in'/'new-arriv'/'just-in'. Two of the 14 (girls-new-in, boys-new-in) returned SSR 'initialItems': [] (0 products) and were dropped per the zero-product-listing rule. This project is company-wide (the brief has no home-decor-only scope restriction), so New Arrivals listings from all departments were checked and included, not just home-decor items. Counts came from the site's own server-rendered 'initialItems' JSON blob (page-0 grid, 48-item cap): array length <48 = exact total (established technique from the prior Home-Decor pass on this exact site). 5 pages hit the 48-item cap (all-new-in, baby-new-in, nightwear-new-in, new-in-accessories, new-in-home-accessories); their true totals came from WebFetch's rendered 'Showing 48 of Y' text. 'All New In' (561) is kept as a genuine parent/umbrella row (is_group=true) alongside the 12 kept department children as siblings, per Rule 0.6/overlap-is-expected precedent from the prior Home-Decor pass on this site (Lighting + its Ceiling Lights/Table Lamps sub-URLs) - the children's counts sum to well under 561 so this is consistent with All New In being a genuine broader aggregate, not a duplicate/alias of any one child. children-and-baby-new-in (qty 3, toys-and-books items) was inspected directly - its SSR items are genuine newly-added toy products, so kept unflagged despite its generic-sounding page title.
